label: Area Chart
description: A single line filled down to the axis with a fading gradient.
howTo: Bind `xAxis.data` to the category or time labels and `series[0].data` to numbers.
The fill is a top-to-bottom gradient in `series[0].areaStyle.color`; its two colours are fixed and do not follow the theme. Replace `areaStyle` with `{}` for a plain fill in the series colour.

label: Stacked Area
description: Several series stacked on top of each other as filled bands, with the total labelled on top.
howTo: All series share `stack: "Total"`, so each band sits on the one before and the top edge is the sum. Bind each `series[n].data` to numbers aligned with `xAxis.data`.
Only the last series shows labels. They show that series alone, not the total.

label: Smoothed Line
description: Curved lines through the points instead of straight segments.
howTo: `smooth: true` curves the line between points. Use a number from 0 to 1 for less curvature. Bind `series[n].data` and `xAxis.data` as for any line.
`yAxis.scale: true` lets the axis start near the data instead of at zero.

label: Step Line
description: Values held between samples. Three series show the three step modes: start, middle and end.
howTo: `step` decides where the line jumps: `"end"` holds a value until the next sample, which is how a tag value behaves between changes. Use `"start"` or `"middle"` for the other conventions.
Bind `series[n].data` to numbers aligned with `xAxis.data`, or to `[timestamp, value]` pairs with `xAxis.type` set to `"time"`.

label: Limits and Operating Bands
description: A process value over a day with high and low limit lines, a shaded operating range and a highlighted time window.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data` to the process values and `xAxis.data` to the time labels.
The limit lines are `series[0].markLine.data[n].yAxis`: bind each to a setpoint tag. The label template `High {c}` prints the bound value.

The bands are pairs in `series[0].markArea.data`: `[{yAxis: low}, {yAxis: high}]` for a value range across the chart, `[{xAxis: from}, {xAxis: to}]` for a time window. The `xAxis` values must be labels that exist in `xAxis.data`.

label: Live Bar + Line (Dual Axis)
description: Bars and a line on two value axes over a short time window. The sample data is static: bind xAxis.data and each series data to tag history or a rolling dataset to make it live.
howTo: Meant for live data. Bind `xAxis.data` to a list of time labels and `series[0].data` / `series[1].data` to lists of numbers of the same length, for example the last N rows of a tag-history binding polled every few seconds.
A rolling window is easiest to keep in a custom property: append the new sample and drop the oldest in a tag change script, then bind the three paths to that property.
Leave the component's `notMerge` off so each update animates from the previous values. `animationDurationUpdate` sets how long that takes.
Remove the fixed `min` and `max` of each `yAxis` entry if your ranges are not known in advance.

label: Line Coloured by Threshold
description: One line whose colour changes with the value: green in range, amber on warning, red above the alarm limit.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data` to the values. The colour ranges are in `visualMap.pieces`: bind the `lt` / `gte` limits to your warning and alarm setpoints.
The dashed lines repeat the same limits in `series[0].markLine.data[n].yAxis`. Bind them to the same setpoints so the two stay together.

label: Time Series with Zoom
description: A filled line on a real time axis with a zoom slider and mouse-wheel zoom, for trends of timestamped values.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data` to a list of `[timestamp, value]` pairs, with timestamps in milliseconds since 1970. No `xAxis.data` is needed on a time axis.
`dataZoom` `start` and `end` are percentages of the full range. The first entry is wheel and drag zoom, the second the slider.
`sampling: "lttb"` thins the points drawn when there are more of them than pixels, so long histories stay fast.
